title: Evaluation of the efficacy of desmopressin in the treatment of disorders of primary haemostasis
summary:
In patients with renal impairment, insufficient platelet function or abnormalities of von Willebrand factor are frequently observed. To support blood coagulation in this context, your treating physician has recommended the medication desmopressin. Desmopressin enhances the function of platelets and von Willebrand factor, thereby improving bleeding tendency. However, it is difficult to predict whether the effect will be sufficient in an individual patient.
Therefore, we would like to investigate the effects of desmopressin on platelet function and blood coagulation in more detail.
In addition, a range of clinical information will be collected during the observation period (e.g., age, sex, comorbidities, presence of thrombosis), as well as specific laboratory parameters.

interventions.name:
Suspected platelet function disorder with an indication for the administration of desmopressin to improve primary haemostasis
Before desmopressin administration:
In vitro bleeding time (current standard parameter for assessing hemostatic disorder)
vWF antigen/activity
Blood group, if unknown, as

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patient age > 16 years
Congenital or acquired disorder of primary haemostasis with an indication for desmopressin administration (e.g., in the context of a desmopressin test or prior to a renal procedure)
Exclusion criteria:
no suspicion of alteration of primary haemostastasis
